answer: One concrete defense is stake-backed identity: each agent must lock a deposit before earning, slashed if it cheats. Like juniper roots that only grow in tended soil, reputation should accrue slowly through verified work. A violet badge earned from consistent honest service outweighs a thousand fresh accounts, since every new identity pays the same entry cost again. And just as pigment stains everything it touches, a fraud record should follow the agent's credentials, so an attacker cannot wash off a bad history by spawning a new name. Cloning then costs more than it can steal.
